Boston has about 1,200 public cameras.
Nobody is watching them live.

Today

Footage gets pulled after something happens.

People hear about incidents through group chats and rumors.

With Revere

The model flags incidents while they’re happening.

An official checks each one before it goes on the public map.

Camera count: Boston Globe (2024), about 1,300; ACLU and City of Boston report, 1,153 (July 2024)

How it works

The detector can run on a separate PC. It only needs the backend’s IP address.

5

The model on real footage

Four test clips running through the detector at the same time.

  • Red means an incident was flagged, with a severity score out of 5.
  • Green means normal activity and no alert.
  • The yellow line shows the chance that a crime might be happening.
  • The graph under each feed tracks the alert level over the clip.
